claim: For the 3-uniform hypergraph \(F_5\) with edges \(\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\},\{c,d,e\}\) on five distinct vertices, every \(F_5\)-free 3-uniform hypergraph on six vertices has at most \(10\) edges, with equality if and only if it consists of all triples containing one fixed vertex; hence \(\operatorname{ex}_3(6,F_5)=10\) and the six labeled extremizers form one isomorphism class.

correctness.rationale: The star construction is \(F_5\)-free and has exactly \(\binom{5}{2}=10\) edges. The embedded verifier exhausts all \(2^{20}\) labeled 3-graphs, all 180 distinct forbidden \(F_5\) masks, and all \(720\) vertex permutations for extremizer canonicalization. It finds maximum 10, exactly six labeled extremizers, verifies all six stars are extremal, and finds one isomorphism class. The proof is confined to \(n=6\).

value.rationale: This is a natural exact small-order boundary for the classical \(F_5\) Turan problem. At \(n=6\), the unique extremizer is a 10-edge star, whereas the balanced complete tripartite 3-graph \(T_3(6,3)\) has 8 edges; the finite result records a concrete exceptional regime before the eventual construction. The exact computation is fully reproducible and the claim is appropriately limited to \(n=6\).
